column2: The lightest element with no stable isotopes, and the first made artificially (1937): its name comes from the Greek for 'artificial'. Technetium-99m is used in tens of millions of medical scans a year.

Element 118, the last on the table, named after Yuri Oganessian: only the second element named after a living person. Only a handful of atoms have ever been made, each gone in under a millisecond, which makes it a favourite answer for sounding obscure.
